*2011 Big 12 All-Rookie Team }} '''Tristan Trevor James Thompson''' (born March 13, 1991 in [[Brampton]], [[Ontario]]) is a [[Canada|Canadian]] [[basketball]] player from who played for the [[2010–11 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team]]. He is 6'8" and weighs 225 pounds. Thompson played as a [[Cornerman (basketball)|cornerman]].{{cite news|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/tristan-thompson}} ==Early life== Thompson was born in [[Brampton]], [[Ontario]], and is the oldest of four brothers of Trevor and Andrea Thompson. He is also the cousin of fellow NCAA athlete and former [[Virginia State University]] Trojan football standout Jemal Thompson.{{cite news|url=http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/thompson_tristan00.html}} ==High school career== Thompson started his high-school career playing basketball at [[St. Marguerite d'Youville Secondary School]] in [[Brampton]], [[Ontario]], [[Canada]]. After driving from [[Brampton]] twice to visit a prep school in the [[United States]], he decided to attend [[Saint Benedict's Preparatory School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]] for his sophomore year along with fellow [[University of Texas at Austin]] commit [[Myck Kabongo]]. He cited the increase in exposure and skill level as his reason for transferring schools.{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/kevin_armstrong/02/26/tristan.thompson/index.html | work=CNN | title=Canadian prospects searching for more exposure at American schools | date=February 27, 2009}} Thompson spent his sophomore and half his junior year at St. Benedict's, making an immediate impact and showing flashes of brilliance throughout the way.{{cite news|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Top-High-School-Prospects-at-the-2007-City-of-Palms-Classic-2421}} In his short time at St. Benedict's, he shot through the ranks to superstardom, becoming the top recruit in the nation entering his junior season.{{cite news|url=http://www.basketball.ca/en/hm/inside.php?sid=1&id=2336}} The top basketball programs in the nation heavily sought Thompson, who made the first verbal commitment of the class of 2010 to [[Rick Barnes]] and the [[Texas Longhorns]].{{cite news|url=http://grassrootsballin.wordpress.com/2008/03/04/tristan-thompson-st-benedicts-nj-class-of-2010-picks-texas}} 21 games into his junior year, the relationship between Thompson and then-St. Benedict's coach-[[Dan Hurley]] hit a rough patch. Hurley's in-your-face, no holds barred coaching style took a toll on the young star. During a game against then-top-ranked [[Mater Dei]], Hurley confronted Thompson during a time out. A heated debate ensued, and Thompson was sent off the court and later removed from the team.{{cite news|url=http://blog.nj.com/hssportsextra/2009/02/texas_recruit_tristan_thompson.html}} Over the next few days he made it known that he was planning to leave, resulting in a barrage of calls from the top prep schools throughout [[North America]], all trying to acquire the top recruit's services. The next week he transferred to Findlay Prep with his friend, AAU teammate and future Texas Longhorn [[Cory Joseph]].{{cite news|url=http://www.torontosun.com/sports/columnists/steve_simmons/2009/02/13/8375606-sun.html}}{{cite news|url=http://insidetexas.com/news/story.php?article=838}} Thompson joined Findlay on the back end of their schedule, making an immediate impact on the team and thriving under Findlay Coach [[Michael Peck]]'s system and coaching style. Thompson solidified his top recruit status and helped lead Findlay to their first National Championship. He continued to round and polish his skills his senior year in preparation for college and continued to hold fast to his commitment to the University of Texas, officially signing his letter of intent on November 11, 2009.{{cite news|url=http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111109aaa.html}} Thompson then led his team to another National Championship at the ESPN National Championship Invitational.{{cite news|url=http://www.espnmediazone3.com/us/2010/04/findlay-prep-repeats-at-the-second-annual-espn-rise-national-high-school-invitational-%E2%80%93-corey-joseph-mvp/}} After their senior year, Thompson and Joseph were the second and third Canadians to be named [[McDonald's All-American|McDonald's All-Americans]],{{cite news|url=http://blogs.canoe.ca/courtside/general/tristan-thompson-and-cory-joseph-make-mcdonalds-all-american-team-nba-trade-chatter}} and Thompson also was named a Jordan Brand Classic All-American.{{cite news|url=http://www.nike.com/jumpman23/classic/2010roster.html}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2010}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Tristan Thompson | position = [[Small forward|SF]], [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = Brampton, Ontario | highschool = [[The Henderson International School|Findlay Prep]] (NV) | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 225 | 40 = | commitdate = March 4, 2008 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | espn grade = 97 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | year = 2010 | rivals ref title = Texas Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2010 Texas Basketball Commits | espn ref title = ESPN | rivals school = 83 | scout s = 110 | espn schoolid = 251 | scout overall = 3 (PF) | rivals overall = 17; 6 (PF) | espn overall = 10; 4 (PF) | accessdate = May 18, 2011 | bball = yes }} ==College career== *[[2011 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans]]: [[Associated Press]] Honorable Mention
